Definition: from G2040; occupation; by implication, profit, pains:--craft, diligence, gain, work.
BiblicalUsage: Ergasía is work — the occupation, the business, the doing. The masters of the damsel made much gain by her divination; Demetrius the silversmith made silver shrines; and Paul says the Gentiles gave themselves over to work all uncleanness with greediness. It is the word for what a person does for a living — and for what it does to them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ergasía shows that work is never neutral: the same word covers honest trade and the gain of soothsayers. I hold that what I do for a living must be work God can bless, not work that profits from sin.
